movement_source: row 'Net interest margin (%)', column Full Year Ended 30 Jun 25 -> column Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26
headline: CBA's Group net interest margin fell 3bpts to 2.05% in FY26 from 2.08% in FY25 (KPI table, cash basis; FY25 book prints the same 2.08%). Net interest income still rose $1,563m or 7% to $25,586m, driven by an 8% ($92bn) rise in average interest earning assets to $1,246bn, "partly offset by a 3 basis point decrease in net interest margin". The bank frames the decline as essentially technical: "Excluding growth in liquid assets, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, net interest margin was stable" — average liquid assets grew to $187,337m from $172,050m. Underlying, lower lending margins from competition (-5bpts) were offset by replicating-portfolio and capital hedge earnings (+5bpts) and favourable business-lending/deposit mix (+2bpts), with liquids (-3bpts) and Treasury & Markets (-2bpts) taking the margin down. The slide walk (p60) publishes the same 208→205 with slightly different bar cuts (Liquids & repos -4, Treasury & Markets -1).

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year to Jun 26 Full Year
drivers.narrative: Largest single drag. The bank says margin was stable "Excluding growth in liquid assets, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income"; average liquid assets rose to $187,337m from $172,050m (+9%). The slide splits the drag as liquid assets (3) and institutional repos (1), with "Minimal impact on earnings".

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year to Jun 26 Full Year
drivers.narrative: "Decreased margin by 5 basis points driven by home lending pricing (down 4 basis points) and business and institutional lending pricing (down 1 basis point), primarily reflecting the impact of competition." The slide sub-splits this as home loan competition (3), impact of cash rate lag (1), Business & Insto. lending (1).

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year to Jun 26 Full Year
drivers.narrative: The bank publishes a zero bar and states "Funding costs: Flat." — an explicit statement that funding costs contributed nothing to the full-year movement, corroborated by the slide's zero bar. No sub-drivers or offsets are disclosed for the full year.

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year to Jun 26 Full Year
drivers.narrative: "Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by favourable asset mix from strong growth in business lending and favourable funding mix from strong growth in deposits." The slide annotates it as "Favourable asset mix and deposits growing faster than lending". Business and corporate average loans rose 10% to $299bn.

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year to Jun 26 Full Year
drivers.narrative: The results book prints a zero bar and states "Basis risk: Flat." — the bills/OIS spread contributed nothing to the FY26 movement. The presentation walk does not publish a separate basis risk bar at all, so this bar is disclosed only in the results book.

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year to Jun 26 Full Year
drivers.narrative: Largest positive. "Increased margin by 5 basis points driven by higher earnings on the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 4 basis points) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 1 basis point)." The slide labels the same +5 bar "Interest rate risk hedging", split replicating portfolio 4 / higher earnings on capital 1.

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year to Jun 26 Full Year
drivers.narrative: "Decreased margin by 2 basis points due to lower risk management income in Treasury and growth in reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances." Repo growth also sits behind the slide's liquids bar (+$11bn average institutional repos), so the split of repo drag between this bar and liquids differs between the two documents (slide shows -1 here).

disagreements.topic: Liquids bar size (results book -3 vs slide -4)
disagreements.explanation: The slide's bar bundles institutional repo drag (1bpt) into liquids, while the results book leaves repo growth inside Treasury & Markets. Same 208->205 endpoints; the results book framing is adopted per source hierarchy.

disagreements.topic: Treasury & Markets bar size (results book -2 vs slide -1)
disagreements.explanation: Mirror image of the liquids difference: the repo-balance drag is allocated to Treasury & Markets in the book and to 'Liquids & repos' on the slide. Both walks sum to -3bpts.

values: Flat / 0 bps bar published (profit announcement p28)
No basis risk bar published (results presentation p60)
disagreements.explanation: The slide walk has six bars and omits basis risk entirely; the results book publishes seven bars including an explicit flat basis risk. Since it is zero, the two walks reconcile.

limitations: The bank qualifies the headline decline heavily: it says margins were 'broadly stable' excluding liquid asset and institutional repo growth, which have 'broadly neutral impacts on net interest income' - so the -3bpt reported fall overstates the economic margin pressure, and the liquids/repo bars carry 'Minimal impact on earnings'.

The two published walks for FY25->FY26 allocate the repo drag differently (liquids -3/T&M -2 in the book vs liquids&repos -4/T&M -1 on the slide); the results book framing is adopted and the slide bars are not mixed in.

The 'Funding costs: Flat' and 'Basis risk: Flat' bars are net zeros with no gross components disclosed for the full year; the half-on-half commentary (funding +2bpts from rising rates partly offset by unfavourable deposit mix) belongs to the Dec 25 -> Jun 26 half comparison and is not used here.
Sub-splits inside asset pricing differ between documents (book: home lending -4, business/institutional -1; slide: home loan competition -3, cash rate lag -1, business & insto -1). Both total -5.

evidence_records.quote: [walk chart] NIM Movement since June 2025: Jun 25 Full Year 208.0 -> Jun 26 Full Year 205.0
Net interest margin (%) 2.05 2.08 (3)bpts 2.06 2.04 2 bpts
Presented on a cash basis unless stated otherwise.

Net interest income was $25,586 million, an increase of $1,563 million or 7% on the prior year. The result was driven by a $92 billion or 8% increase in average interest earning assets to $1,246 billion, partly offset by a 3 basis point decrease in net interest margin to 2.05%.

The Bank's net interest margin decreased by 3 basis points on the prior year to 2.05%. Excluding growth in liquid assets, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, net interest margin was stable.

Asset pricing: Decreased margin by 5 basis points driven by home lending pricing (down 4 basis points) and business and institutional lending pricing (down 1 basis point), primarily reflecting the impact of competition.
Funding costs: Flat.
Portfolio mix: Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by favourable asset mix from strong growth in business lending and favourable funding mix from strong growth in deposits.
Basis risk: Flat.

Capital, Replicating and Other: Increased margin by 5 basis points driven by higher earnings on the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 4 basis points) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 1 basis point).
